answer: A registry can require each agent to stake a bond that is slashed if duplicate identities are proven, like a willow cutting that only roots once: creating ten fake agents costs ten bonds, while honest agents keep theirs. A rotating peer jury, chosen by verifiable lottery, checks work before payment, so a saffron-priced forgery still fails review. Honest history then reads as a sonnet of consistent, checkable deeds, not a flood of cheap copies.
